title: 5  Methodological moderators
text: 5 Methodological moderators Code Show All Code Hide All Code View Source This section presents methodological moderators that may influence estimates of mixed-paternity prevalence across studies. We focus on marker type, nest-box use, nest type, and study duration, because these variables can affect both the detection and reporting of mixed paternity. All models use the same multilevel phylogenetic beta-binomial structure as the overall model. Model-based prevalence is summarised as the posterior mean on the probability scale, with 95% equal-tailed credible intervals. The inverse-logit transformation is applied to each posterior draw before averaging; all random effects are set to zero. 5.1 Packages The R packages required for model fitting. DNA fingerprinting studies had lower estimated mixed-paternity prevalence than microsatellite, SNP and mixed/other studies in the single-moderator comparisons. These are comparative associations among studies; the category-specific prevalence intervals and the pairwise contrasts answer different questions. The primary multivariable model also retained higher prevalence for each of the other marker categories relative to DNA fingerprinting after adjustment for the other moderators.

The lower reported prevalence in DNA fingerprinting studies is consistent with underdetection of mixed-paternity broods by this older method and, consequently, possible underestimation of their prevalence. This does not directly establish differences in detection sensitivity or quantify detection bias. Marker type is associated with study era, taxonomic composition, candidate-parent sampling, genotyping completeness, exclusion power, error checking and parentage-assignment criteria. The mixed/other category is heterogeneous and should not be interpreted as one newer technology.

title: 1  Overview
text: Evolutionary history strongly structures brood-level mixed paternity across birds Author Aneta Arct 1,2* , Santiago Ortega 1 , Szymon M. Drobniak 2 , Agnieszka Gudowska 3 , Karolina Skorb 4 , Monika Gronowska 5 , Magdalena Zagalska-Neubauer 5 , Michael Griesser 6 , Malgorzata Lagisz 1,† , Shinichi Nakagawa 1,† This website presents the complete reproducible workflow for the global comparative meta-analysis of mixed-paternity prevalence across birds. Studies using microsatellites, single-nucleotide polymorphisms or mixed/other marker systems reported higher mixed-paternity prevalence than those using DNA fingerprinting, suggesting that the older method may underestimate its prevalence. title: 4  Overall model
text: 4.4 Modelling framework Because brood-level paternity data are expected to exhibit substantial extra-binomial heterogeneity across references, populations, and species, we modelled mixed-paternity prevalence using beta-binomial generalised linear mixed-effects models with a logit link: \[y_i \sim \mathrm{BetaBinomial}(n_i, \mu_i, \phi)\] where \(y_i\) is the number of broods with mixed paternity, \(n_i\) is the total number of broods genotyped, \(\mu_i\) is the expected mixed-paternity prevalence, and the precision parameter \(\phi\) describes extra-binomial variation among study units. For models with a population-level intercept, the linear predictor was: \[\mathrm{logit}(\mu_i) = \alpha + \mathbf{X}_i \boldsymbol{\beta} + u_{\mathrm{reference}[i]} + u_{\mathrm{species}[i]} + u_{\mathrm{phylo}[i]}\] where \(\alpha\) is the intercept, \(\mathbf{X}_i \boldsymbol{\beta}\) represents fixed biological and methodological moderators, and \(u_{\mathrm{reference}}\) , \(u_{\mathrm{species}}\) , and \(u_{\mathrm{phylo}}\) represent study-identifier-level, non-phylogenetic species-level, and phylogenetically structured random effects, respectively. Study identifier ( Study_ID ) is an analytical grouping variable, not a bibliographic-publication count; one study identifier can incorporate evidence reported across more than one source. The single-moderator models for marker type, nest type, BG breeding system, BIRDBASE mating system, and parental care use 0 + category : each fitted category has its own logit coefficient, with no shared population-level intercept or reference category. Pairwise contrasts subtract category coefficients within each posterior draw. The primary multivariable model and binary single-moderator models instead use an intercept and reference-category contrasts. All models retain the three random-intercept terms. 4.4.1 Model coding and priors Reference categories apply only to models with a population-level intercept. Primary = primary multivariable model; single = single-moderator model; both = both model types. The five models fitted with 0 + category have no reference category. Population-level intercept Student-t(3, 0, 2.5) Models with a shared population-level intercept only; absent from the five 0 + category models. Beta-binomial precision (phi) Gamma(0.01, 0.01), positive All models; shape–rate parameterisation. These priors were verified in the saved fits. The Intercept prior applies to the internally centred intercept used by brms, where applicable; it does not apply to category logits in 0 + category models. Flat priors are improper, so the complete specification should not be described collectively as weakly informative. Priors are on group-level SDs; posterior heterogeneity is reported as variance by squaring each SD draw. See the brms prior documentation .

text: Matched-sample model without moderators This additional intercept-only model provides a matched-sample reference for the final multivariable model (Supplementary Table S12). It uses exactly the same 533 observations from 481 study identifiers and 326 species. It is distinct from the overall model above, which uses the full dataset of 619 observations; it is not a replacement estimate of overall mixed-paternity prevalence. The response is the number of mixed-paternity broods out of the total number of broods, modelled with a beta-binomial distribution and a logit link. The matched model includes an intercept and random intercepts for study identifier, non-phylogenetic species identity, and phylogenetically structured species identity, with no moderators. The data, phylogenetic covariance matrix, grouping structure and corresponding priors are retained from the final multivariable model. Priors are Student-t(3, 0, 2.5) for the intercept and group-level standard deviations (restricted to positive values for standard deviations), and Gamma(0.01, 0.01), in shape-rate notation, for beta-binomial precision. Load prepared objects Model Results The null model was fitted on Totoro with four chains, 10,000 iterations per chain including 5,000 warmup iterations (20,000 retained draws), seed 20261015, adapt_delta = 0.99 and max_treedepth = 15. The existing final multivariable model was not refitted. The table reports posterior mean variances and equal-tailed 95% credible intervals on the logit scale. Each posterior standard-deviation draw was squared before summarising; the sum was calculated within each model draw.
